source.title: StitchNet: Composing Neural Networks from Pre-Trained Fragments
source.authors: Surat Teerapittayanon; Marcus Z. Comiter; Bradley McDanel; H.-T. Kung

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether fragments from different pretrained networks can be joined using a projection and produce useful stitched networks. This bears on interchangeability through stitching, though it does not directly measure representation loss against an unstiched counterpart.
record.gate_note: The study reports CKA compatibility scores and downstream task accuracy for stitched networks. Its discussion of universal features cites prior work and is not a result of this study.
record.test_reason: StitchNet uses cross-network linear stitching as a tool for building task-specific classifiers. It reports only its own method's downstream accuracy against off-the-shelf networks. Its best rows are picked from 89 generated StitchNets on the test results. It never measures how much is lost when one network's representation is mapped onto another's, compared with the unstitched network on the same function. The universality discussion (Sec. IV-A, V) cites prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that StitchNet composes networks from CKA-selected fragments of different pretrained models via a fused pseudoinverse projection, without retraining. They report comparable or higher accuracy on personalized tasks, using far less data and compute than fine-tuning or training from scratch.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses linear CKA to guide fragment selection and a pseudoinverse-derived projection fused into the next fragment's weights; it does not reproduce a method from the cited convergence studies.

fits_no_version.finding: Fragments of five ImageNet CNNs (alexnet, densenet121, mobilenet_v3_small, resnet50, vgg16) can be chained across architectures using a least-squares linear projection fitted on 32 samples, with no retraining. The 89 generated StitchNets reach 0.67–0.95 accuracy on Dogs vs. Cats (Fig. 3a). High product-CKA (>0.9) goes with high accuracy, but not the reverse.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-free linear stitching across architectures yields functional task-specific networks, and CKA between fragment activations predicts stitch success.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications
record.problems: The reported stitched-network results are task-specific downstream accuracies, not direct measurements of representation loss relative to an unstiched counterpart. The Food101 comparison is described in text but exact values are not stated there.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports 89 generated StitchNets and summary plots in Sec. III-C and Fig. 3, plus per-network plots in Figs. 4 and 7; individual values for most generated networks are not stated in text or tabulated clearly enough to extract separately. Fine-tuning comparisons in Fig. 6 concern data/computation requirements rather than directly measuring representational interchangeability.

untested.parts: No vision-language or paired image-caption data.
No measured loss of a linear map or stitch relative to the unstitched network. Relative representations and unpaired mapping are not tested.
No variation of the similarity measure or of input distribution as a test of convergence.
No test of a plateau or of shared data or objectives as the cause.

missing.what: Distribution of accuracy and CKA across all 89 generated StitchNets (not just the selected best), relevant if the stitching-functionality claim is tracked.

record.verdict_notes: The study is an engineering and application paper. Its better-than-pretrained accuracies reflect task personalization: the pretrained models were not trained for these specific classes, as the authors say in Sec. III-D. They do not show that representations are interchangeable. The CKA values in the tables for single pretrained models (e.g. 0.99, 1.00) show the score is a pipeline heuristic rather than a cross-model similarity measure.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model scale or capability, nor test of convergence as models grow.
No paired image-caption data or vision-language models.
No comparison of independently initialized networks of the same architecture.

Tests stitching with paired target-dataset samples and a projection, but not direct representation loss against an unstiched model; does not test relative representations or stitching without paired data.
No analysis of recurring interpretable features or circuits.
Does not compare alternative similarity measures or systematically vary similarity settings or input distributions.
Does not test whether alignment plateaus or whether shared training data or objectives explain it.

rows.subject: best_stitchnet
rows.operation_detail: Stitched fragments using a projection derived from target-dataset activations
rows.note: The paper reports this as the best StitchNet; the table gives 8.0M parameters and an overall CKA score of 0.91.
rows.check: Selection value: the best of 89 StitchNets, compared with pretrained ImageNet models on a remapped two-class task. This is the study's method versus others, not a measure of mapping loss. Its 8.0M params and 2841M MACs equal densenet121's, so its fragment makeup is unclear.

rows.subject: best_stitchnet
rows.operation_detail: Reported overall CKA score for the stitched network
rows.note: CKA is used by the paper as a compatibility measure for stitching.
rows.check: The overall CKA score is the product of per-stitch CKAs, used as a compatibility heuristic for selection. It has no baseline and cannot show whether the version's effect appears.

rows.subject: StitchNet27
rows.operation_detail: Stitched fragments using a projection derived from target-dataset activations
rows.note: The paper explicitly compares StitchNet27 with pretrained alexnet.
rows.check: A hand-picked StitchNet compared with alexnet on task accuracy. The study's method versus others; it does not measure representational mapping loss.

rows.subject: StitchNet27
rows.operation_detail: Reported overall CKA score for the stitched network
rows.note: The table reports this score alongside the accuracy and model size.
rows.check: The overall CKA is a selection heuristic with no baseline. Not a measure of cross-model convergence.

rows.subject: best_stitchnet

rows.subject: best_stitchnet

rows.subject: top-performing StitchNets
rows.operation_detail: Stitched fragments for five three-class Food101 tasks
rows.measure: accuracy relative to original pretrained networks
rows.value: Top-performing StitchNets surpass all original pretrained networks in all tasks; exact values not stated in text
rows.note: The text states the comparison across all five tasks but provides no exact accuracy values.
rows.check: Figure-only comparison of the top StitchNet per task (selected) against pretrained networks. No values are given, and it is the method's own performance.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
